messages:
lina (marketing): Folks, we need a tight benchmark narrative for next week's launch email + webinar. Goal: show latency predictability + unit cost savings without claiming 'cheapest'.

raj (growth): Keep the hero stat simple: one sentence in subject line mentioning p95 and $/1M tokens. e.g., 'Predictable p95 latency ~150ms and 2.5x lower unit cost for common chat workloads'.

tess (product): Let's define workloads: live chat (short-turn, 32 token responses) and long-context generation (2k tokens). Different SLOs make the trade clear.

mike (data): Proposed sample numbers (placeholders):
```
workload,model,median_ms,p95_ms,cost_per_1M
chat,redwood-v2,50,130,95
chat,redwood-v2-quant,70,170,40
chat/open,open-llm,110,300,210
long,redwood-v2,180,420,240
```
Use median+p95 and $/1M tokens.

anya (design): Visual idea: stacked micro-tiles for each workload. Each tile shows median bar, p95 whisker, and a small cost badge. Also a separate scatter: p95 vs cost with workload color coding.

lina (marketing): Messaging lines: 1) problem: model serving costs and latency vary wildly; 2) solution: runtime + controls (batching, KV cache, routing) that reduce cost variance; 3) evidence: benchmark charts; 4) CTA: signup for webinar + workload calc.

raj (growth): Lead routing: webinar form with a checkbox "Interested in Dedicated" -> if checked tag as 'enterprise-hot' in HubSpot and create SFDC lead. Others go to nurture sequence + trial credits.

mike (data): Chart notes: show both absolute and relative numbers. Include an inset table with % cost reduction vs baseline. And annotate one row showing how quantization affects latency under heavy throughput.

tess (product): Add a short technical sidebar in the post: benchmarking methodology (request pattern, batch sizes, instance types, warm vs cold, SDK version). Transparency builds trust. Keep the sidebar collapsed in the blog but visible in the webinar.

anya (design): For accessibility, avoid relying solely on color. Use patterns/markers for workloads and include numeric labels on the badges.

lina (marketing): Webinar angle: 'From Unpredictable to Predictable: How Teams Cut Latency Variance and Unit Cost'. Structure: 10m problem, 15m demo + live bench, 10m customer panel, 15m Q&A.

leadbot: Registered 12 attendees so far from the early list.

raj (growth): Can we add a short calculator link: "Estimate your monthly inference spend" — drives conversions. Needs a simple API to estimate tokens * traffic * $/1M. I can spec the form.

mike (data): I'll generate the final CSV and charts by Tue EOD. Also will include error bars on p95 when sample size is low.

anya (design): I'll produce hero image + three chart PNGs for social + slides by Wed noon.

lina (marketing): Copy iteration: I'll draft 3 subject lines and a 250-word blog draft by Tue. Then we do one round of edits Wed morning.

tess (product): Quick copy tweak: emphasize "controls you can tune" (batching/cache/quant/routing) rather than implying magic.

lina (marketing): Action items summary:
- mike: finalize numbers & export charts (due Tue EOD)
- anya: hero + PNGs + slide assets (due Wed noon)
- raj: signup + HubSpot/SFDC mapping + calc spec (due Wed)
- tess: methodology sidebar + product callouts (due Tue)
- lina: blog draft + subject lines (due Tue)

leadbot: Webinar page draft created: /marketing/webinars/predictable-inference.

lina (marketing): Great work. We'll reconvene Thu 9am PT for a dry run. If anyone needs to shift due dates, ping here. :rocket:
